## Claims
- [source-backed] Theorem 5.4 assumes \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\) bigrassmannian in type \(A_{n-1}\), \(\mathfrak S_v=s_{i^j}\), and defines \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\). It gives
  \[
  \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\},\qquad
  \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\},
  \]
  and states that each has \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements. [source-2, lines 1380-1421]
- [proved] Under the requested notation \(p=n-r-i=c=r-j=2\), with \(i=j=2\), one has \(a=b=2\). The two source families specialize exactly to
  \[
  \mathcal F_1=\{s_{22},s_{32},s_{42},s_{33},s_{43},s_{44}\},
  \qquad
  \mathcal F_2=\{s_{22},s_{221},s_{222},s_{2211},s_{2221},s_{2222}\}.
  \]
  Indeed their respective upper shapes are \((4^2)=(4,4)\) and \((2^2,2^2)=(2,2,2,2)\); enumerating the partitions in each indicated Young interval gives the displayed six shapes. Their common cardinality is
  \[
  \binom{a+b}{a}=\binom42=6.
  \]
- [unsupported] The inspected theorem does not use the symbols \(p,c\); the identification \(p=n-r-i\), \(c=r-j\) is required to translate the requested specialization into its parameters.
